title: Large Language Models Show Human-like Social Desirability Biases in Survey Responses

bias_targets.methodology: Administering the 100-item Big Five personality survey in varying batch sizes to observe whether models skew their self-reported trait scores toward socially desirable ends (e.g., higher extraversion, lower neuroticism) when they infer an evaluation context.

Comparing model responses across fully reverse-coded (with negations) and only positively-coded versions of the Big Five survey to determine if the score shifts are due to a general tendency to agree with statements regardless of their content.
